notes: COMMON-NAME RISK HANDLED AS INSTRUCTED. 'Akshay Singh' is a very common North Indian name and the input row carried no experience figure, so I required the CARE + Musheerabad + neurosurgery combination to match EXPLICITLY before accepting anything. It does: CARE's own domain returned a per-doctor page titled 'Dr. Akshay Singh | Top Neurosurgeon in Musheerabad | CARE Hospitals' at https://www.carehospitals.com/doctor/hyderabad/care-super-specialty-hospital-musheerabad/akshay-singh-neurosurgeon - the URL itself encodes city (hyderabad), branch (musheerabad) and speciality (neurosurgeon) in one line. That is four identity factors (name + specialty + hospital + branch/city) on the hospital's own site, so 'Ambiguous Match' is not warranted. A second, independent page (his clinic's site) separately states he practises at 'Gurunanak CARE Hospitals, Musheerabad, Hyderabad' - wording that matches the input row's address string almost verbatim, which is strong cross-confirmation that this is the right man. CARE BRANCH SLUG FINDING (requested): yes, CARE treats Musheerabad as its own distinct branch slug. It is 'care-super-specialty-hospital-musheerabad'. Notably, unlike the Banjara Hills case documented in the brief - where /doctor/ uses the bare 'banjara-hills' but /doctor-list/ uses the verbose 'care-hospital-banjara-hills' - Musheerabad uses the SAME verbose slug in BOTH page families (/doctor/hyderabad/care-super-specialty-hospital-musheerabad/... and /doctor-list/hyderabad/care-super-specialty-hospital-musheerabad). Also note CARE brands the unit 'CARE Super Specialty Hospital, Musheerabad' on its own site, while the input row calls it 'Gurunanak CARE Hospitals, Musheerabad' - the same physical unit under an older/local name, not a different hospital. NOT a stale affiliation and NOT an index-coverage gap: the named hospital does publish a live per-doctor page for him, so hospital_profile is populated.
